title: C64, Spectrum and DOS source/reconstruction discovery
summary: Review 28 roots: add fifteen source/reconstruction projects, correct the Kult ASM repository rename and record twelve deferrals or out-of-scope candidates.
notes: Root personally searched the six requested platform families and inspected 28 pinned roots. Fifteen new source/reconstruction/research projects, one canonical Kult repository rename, and twelve deferred/out-of-scope candidates. No discovery worker used. Distinguish original-source preservation, partial research, semantic native editions, register-faithful translations and modern redesigns. No platform quota or full-game claim from assets alone. No upstream code, emulator, compiler, archive or game executed. Legacy source encodings and oversized files are linked but not embedded as byte proofs when exact UTF-8 matching fails. Every selected commit was independently fetched. The retained submission uses only pinned proof identities; source bytes are temporary local review material and the importer retrieves/verifies them on first application.

sources.reason: Adapts annotated BBC MOS 1.20 and BBC BASIC sources to Commodore 64 hardware. Shared CPU does not imply hardware compatibility; repository describes the MOS adaptation as ongoing.

Two distinct implementations: a faithful translation retains original register/stack interfaces, while the clean edition uses semantic functions and typed data records without the Z80 CPU interface. Original memory/data formats persist; clean RNG and optional original-bug compatibility are explicit.
MicroEmacs 4.00 TOS adaptation refreshes the ST52 target for GEMlib/libcmini and the French Atari keyboard. Encryption and abbreviations are deliberately disabled to reduce executable size.

Research compares save layouts from independent 1oom and zappatic sources, locates original executable tables and reconstructs Borland overlay addressing. AI-slider notes distinguish equivalent recovered values from omitted table columns.

Address-linked research documents original intro boot flow, resource dispatch, scene containers, mouth animation and PIT timing. Distinguishes numeric resource dispatch from FORM tag interpretation and notes provisional cross-version names.

Documents the AESOP host, script/resource archive and separate dungeon generator, with actual RES/TBL dictionary readers and bytecode tools. Shipped symbols expose original names; game bytecode is distinct from CPU emulation.

Headless CPC hardware emulation supports memory-write, graphics, map and PSG extraction; the concrete Rainbow Islands recipe reconstructs source assets from captured behavior. Emulator is an analysis instrument, not claimed as a native game reconstruction.

Native C++/Direct2D recreation reads original pictures, rooms and collision data. Collision code explicitly traces pose-mask and glyph tests to original addresses; reference disassembly/snapshots are outside the runtime build.

Several ports/reference translations coexist. The Makefile builds src/main.c, while the context describes Central Cavern as the current scope; alternative named-good or assembly-derived files must not be mistaken for the default executable.

Native SDL2 viewer decodes room sizes, location/foreground/background tables and sprites at original binary addresses. Player movement is prototype interaction, not evidence of restored original Knight Lore gameplay.

Source-available remake implements the original building/rescue/explosive objectives and puzzle subgames with new graphics, smooth scrolling, saves and a replacement soundtrack selection. These presentation/features are intentional changes, not byte-exact restoration.

JumPHP remake combines recovered CPC graphics/maps/fonts and recorded PSG audio with new semantic entity/physics code. Assets cover seven islands/28 rounds, but some enemy identities are inferred and bosses on islands 2–6 use enlarged island sprites.
Preserves the commercial OMIKRON.Assembler/TurboAss editor-assembler and Bugaboo debugger source, including binary SRC archives, readable assembly exports and source-format documentation.
Search false positive: Xbox 360 Kinect/avatar emulator work, not DOS or one of the requested platforms.
Atari ST intro conversion, not a game/application reconstruction in this requested pass.
Atari ST intro conversion with replacement soundtrack; not a game/application reconstruction in this requested pass.
Barbarian II cracktro, explicitly not the game and does not launch it. Game title in the name must not create a false game-reconstruction entry.

Atari source-based remake with original and alternate rules, but the ATR-oriented original is outside the requested C64/Spectrum/Amiga/ST/CPC/DOS source-platform focus; retain as adjacent candidate, not a rejection of source quality.
Unity beta with new maze generation; original code recovery or rule-level parity was not established. Defer visual remake rather than claiming faithful restoration.
Very brief browser-remake claim does not establish original data/algorithm recovery or evidence-bearing reconstruction. Needs inspection beyond title-level association before promotion.
MonoGame-style new engine/remake source with no recovered original-format or algorithm provenance established in the inspected tree. Defer rather than equate genre/game homage with restoration.
Explicit redesign with seed-generated caves, new rules and synthetic assets. Distinct modern game rather than original Penetrator restoration; do not infer fidelity from the title.
Repository contains split RAR downloads and a development-plan README, not reviewable game source in the tree. No executable or archive was run; retain as unverified lead.
GitHub old-name API redirects to repository ID 1431143724, matching the new-name root. This is the same matching ASM project, not another addition.

source_updates.reason: Ghidra/IDA workspaces accompany a concrete graphics/sector extractor addressing the captured game image. The useful reviewable deliverable is format/graphics analysis, not a demonstrated complete rebuildable assembly listing.

Developer-hosted archives preserve original development materials, with readable assembly under src including dungeon-map initialization and engine interfaces. README still emphasizes tokenized GFA source in archives; the current tree also has text exports.
Experiment setup and original inputs only; README explicitly says no reversing run has started and no gameplay fidelity exists. Do not promote a planned reconstruction as completed work.
Atari ST demo conversion rather than requested game/application work; preserve as adjacent lead.
